scope: Two H9 classes after first layer 01 23 45: second layers 03 14 67 and 03 16 27. These add two hand cases to the checkpoint's accepted 30/50, yielding 32/50; this does not prove full H9 or the D(18) lower bound.

review.exact_images: Both explicit preimages satisfy the first-layer pair inequalities and produce the target six-vertex fence image. The fixed coordinate map identifies all five poset relations and the independent sorted pair.
review.image_transfer: Conjugating the suffix gives generalized comparator orientations and a fixed output permutation. Prepending the ascending canonical prefix and untangling only the suffix preserves its first two layers; increasing inputs force the final permutation to be identity.
review.third_layer_reduction: The three signed seven-real restrictions collapse the first two layers to two disjoint retained gates. H7 forces three surviving third-layer gates after deleting each edge of path 0-1-3-4. The elementary matching argument forces four gates, with idle 1 and gate 34, or idle 3 and gate 01. Image duality identifies the alternatives. Excluding universally ordered gate 67 leaves twelve third layers.
review.signed_demands: Every listed five-real restriction through layer three has exactly 3-d retained gates, d in {1,2}. If layer four contributed fewer than d, the at-most-two retained gates through layer four could be serialized into two layers before the final three, contradicting the five-wire thin lemma.
review.fourth_layer_coverage: Reviewed the extension, shared-pair and shared-triangle arguments and each of the twelve prose branches against their demand sets and forbidden pairs. Case 10 exhausts only twelve two-edge bases and local one-edge intersections; case 12 uses its forced triangle edge and three collisions. Optional nonmaximal matchings are retained.
review.rank_endings: The attainable-rank interval lemma and remaining-cone bound justify both threshold directions. Reciprocal guard exclusions are necessary for every possible fifth-layer edge, whether or not the partner is mandatory. Thirty forms have an isolated mandatory pivot; the other three have two mandatory pivots sharing only partner 2.
dependencies: The established hand H7 early-profile theorem
The attainable-rank interval and threshold-partner lemmas
Fixed finite rank-input and signed-restriction tables
